items.title: IELTS Academic Test Format
items.summary: Sections, timings, question counts and 2026 delivery changes.

items.title: Band Scores & Marking Criteria
items.summary: Raw-score conversion tables, overall band rounding, writing and speaking criteria.

items.title: Question-Type Strategies
items.summary: How to tackle TFNG, headings, MCQ, completion, maps and more.

items.title: 8-Week Study Plan
items.summary: A week-by-week plan that uses every item in this repo.

items.title: Test Day Checklist
items.summary: What to do the day before and during each section.

items.title: Section 1 · Joining a Sports Centre
items.summary: A phone call to join a leisure centre — form completion with names, numbers and corrections.

items.title: Section 2 · Riverside Museum Tour
items.summary: A guide's introduction to a museum — multiple choice and map labelling.

items.title: Section 3 · Food Waste Research Tutorial
items.summary: Two students and a tutor discuss limitations, findings and how to present data.

items.title: Section 4 · Lecture: Bioluminescence
items.summary: An academic lecture on how and why living things produce light — note completion.

items.title: Section 1 · Reporting Lost Property
items.summary: A phone call to report a bag left on a train — form completion with dates and descriptions.

items.title: Section 2 · Festival Volunteer Briefing
items.summary: A coordinator explains rules and roles to festival volunteers — MCQ and matching.

items.title: Section 3 · Planning a Cycling Presentation
items.summary: Two students plan a presentation on urban cycling policies — MCQ and matching case studies.

items.title: Section 4 · Lecture: Roman Concrete
items.summary: Why Roman concrete has lasted 2,000 years and what modern engineers can learn — note completion.

items.title: Cooling the Concrete Jungle
items.summary: Why cities are hotter than the countryside and what can be done about it.

items.title: The Return of the Wolves
items.summary: The reintroduction of wolves to Yellowstone and the debate over the 'trophic cascade'.

items.title: The Longitude Problem
items.summary: How John Harrison's marine clocks competed with astronomy to solve navigation at sea.

items.title: Why We Sleep on It
items.summary: How different stages of sleep help the brain to store memories.

items.title: Farming Upwards
items.summary: The promise and limits of growing food indoors in stacked layers.

items.title: When a Language Dies
items.summary: Why languages are disappearing, why it matters and how some have been revived.

items.title: Too Much of a Good Thing?
items.summary: The famous jam experiment, 'choice overload' and what later research found.

items.title: The Power of Belief
items.summary: What the placebo effect really is, how big it is, and what makes it stronger.

items.title: Line Graph · International Students in Three Countries
items.summary: Describe and compare trends over 20 years; practise the overview and trend vocabulary.

items.title: Bar Chart · Household Spending 1990 vs 2020
items.summary: Compare proportions across categories and two years; practise grouping data.

items.title: Pie Charts · Electricity Sources 2000 vs 2020
items.summary: Compare two pie charts; describe a shift from coal to gas and renewables.

items.title: Table · Public Transport in Five Cities
items.summary: Select key features from a table with three variables; compare by column.

items.title: Process · Recycling Plastic Bottles
items.summary: Describe a man-made process using the passive voice and sequencers.

items.title: Process · Rainwater Harvesting System
items.summary: Describe a system with a branching end-point; mix active and passive verbs.

items.title: Maps · Westbury Town Centre Then and Now
items.summary: Compare two maps using present perfect passive and location language.

items.title: Mixed Charts · Tourism Arrivals and Purpose of Visit
items.summary: Combine a line graph and bar chart; describe a peak, a collapse and a recovery.

items.title: Bar Chart · Time Online by Age Group
items.summary: Describe absolute vs proportional change across five age groups.

items.title: Maps · Planned Campus Redevelopment
items.summary: Describe planned changes using future passive forms.

items.title: Opinion · Should University Be Free for All?
items.summary: Agree/disagree essay with a partial position and a proposed alternative.

items.title: Discussion · Competition or Cooperation at School?
items.summary: Discuss both views and give your own opinion — classic five-paragraph discussion.

items.title: Advantages & Disadvantages · Working from Home
items.summary: Balanced advantages/disadvantages essay without a required opinion.

items.title: Causes & Solutions · Traffic Congestion
items.summary: Identify causes and match each with a specific solution.

items.title: Two-part Question · Why Are People Moving to Cities?
items.summary: Answer a 'why' question and give a positive/negative verdict.

items.title: Positive or Negative? · More People Living Alone
items.summary: Evaluate a social trend for individuals and for society.

items.title: Opinion · Compulsory Community Service at School
items.summary: Strongly agree essay with a counter-argument and rebuttal paragraph.

items.title: Discussion · Public Money for the Arts?
items.summary: Discuss arts funding vs public services and challenge the either/or premise.

items.title: Opinion · Will AI Replace Teachers?
items.summary: Nuanced disagree essay on technology in education.

items.title: Advantages Outweigh? · International Tourism
items.summary: Weigh advantages against disadvantages and reach a clear verdict.

items.title: Discussion · Who Should Protect the Environment?
items.summary: Individuals vs governments and corporations — link both views into one argument.

items.title: Causes & Solutions · Young People Reading Less
items.summary: Explain a social trend and propose matching, practical solutions.

items.title: Opinion · Should Rich Countries Help Poorer Nations?
items.summary: Agree with a qualification — focus on how aid should be given.

items.title: Two-part Question · Celebrities as Role Models
items.summary: Explain celebrity influence and judge whether it is positive or negative.

items.title: Part 1 · Work or Study
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on work or study with natural model answers.
questions: Do you work or are you a student?
Why did you choose that job / subject?
What do you like most about it?
Is there anything you dislike about it?
Would you like to change your job in the future?

items.title: Part 1 · Hometown
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on hometown with natural model answers.
questions: Where is your hometown?
What do you like about your hometown?
Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
Is it a good place for young people?
Would you like to live there in the future?

items.title: Part 1 · Home & Accommodation
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on home & accommodation with natural model answers.
questions: Do you live in a house or an apartment?
What's your favourite room?
What would you change about your home?
Do you plan to live there for a long time?
What kind of home would you like to live in in the future?

items.title: Part 1 · Free Time & Hobbies
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on free time & hobbies with natural model answers.
questions: What do you like to do in your free time?
How long have you had this hobby?
Do you prefer spending free time alone or with others?
Did you have the same hobbies when you were a child?
Is there a new hobby you'd like to try?

items.title: Part 1 · Weather & Seasons
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on weather & seasons with natural model answers.
questions: What's the weather like where you live?
What's your favourite season?
Does the weather affect your mood?
Do you check the weather forecast?
Has the weather changed since you were a child?

items.title: Part 1 · Food & Cooking
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on food & cooking with natural model answers.
questions: What's your favourite food?
Do you like cooking?
Do you prefer eating at home or eating out?
Is there any food you didn't like as a child but like now?
Do people in your country eat healthily?

items.title: Part 1 · Mobile Phones & Technology
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on mobile phones & technology with natural model answers.
questions: How often do you use your phone?
What do you mainly use it for?
Do you think people spend too much time on their phones?
Have you ever tried to use your phone less?
What was the first phone you had?

items.title: Part 1 · Reading
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on reading with natural model answers.
questions: Do you like reading?
What kind of books do you read?
Do you prefer paper books or e-books?
Did you read a lot as a child?
Do you think children read less now than before?

items.title: Part 1 · Music
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on music with natural model answers.
questions: What kind of music do you like?
When do you usually listen to music?
Can you play a musical instrument?
Have your music tastes changed over time?
Do you prefer live music or recordings?

items.title: Part 1 · Transport & Travel
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on transport & travel with natural model answers.
questions: How do you usually travel to work or school?
Is public transport good where you live?
Do you like travelling?
Where did you go on your last trip?
Where would you like to travel in the future?

items.title: Part 1 · Sleep & Daily Routine
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on sleep & daily routine with natural model answers.
questions: How many hours do you usually sleep?
Are you a morning person or a night person?
What do you do to relax before sleeping?
Do you take naps during the day?
Is your daily routine different at weekends?

items.title: Part 1 · Friends
items.summary: 5 Part 1 questions on friends with natural model answers.
questions: Do you have many friends?
How do you usually spend time with your friends?
Is it easy to make new friends as an adult?
What makes someone a good friend?
Do you prefer having a few close friends or many friends?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Person Who Influenced You
items.summary: Describe a person who has had an important influence on your life.

cue_card.task: Describe a person who has had an important influence on your life.
bullets: how long you have known them
and explain why they have influenced you so much

part3_questions: Who usually has more influence on children — parents or teachers?
Do you think celebrities are good role models for young people?
How has the role of teachers changed in recent years?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Place You Want to Revisit
items.summary: Describe a place you have visited that you would like to go back to.

cue_card.task: Describe a place you have visited that you would like to go back to.
bullets: and explain why you would like to go back

part3_questions: Why do some people prefer to visit the same place again and again?
What are the effects of tourism on natural areas?
Should the number of tourists visiting some places be limited?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Skill You Are Proud Of
items.summary: Describe a skill that you learned and are proud of.

cue_card.task: Describe a skill that you learned and are proud of.
bullets: when and how you learned it
and explain why you are proud of it

part3_questions: What skills do you think children should learn at school apart from academic subjects?
Is it easier to learn new skills as a child or as an adult?
Do you think technology has changed the way people learn skills?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · An Interesting Book
items.summary: Describe a book you read that you found interesting.

cue_card.task: Describe a book you read that you found interesting.
bullets: and explain why you found it interesting

part3_questions: Why do some people prefer reading books to watching films?
Do you think e-books will completely replace printed books?
How can parents encourage children to read more?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Memorable Journey
items.summary: Describe a memorable journey you have made.

cue_card.task: Describe a memorable journey you have made.
bullets: and explain why it was memorable

part3_questions: Do you think people will travel more or less in the future?
What are the advantages of travelling by train rather than by plane?
Why do some people enjoy travelling alone?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Time You Helped Someone
items.summary: Describe a time when you helped someone.

cue_card.task: Describe a time when you helped someone.
bullets: and explain how you felt about helping this person

part3_questions: Why do some people not help others?
Should schools teach children to help others?
Do you think people help each other less than in the past?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Piece of Technology You Use
items.summary: Describe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you use often.

cue_card.task: Describe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you use often.
bullets: and explain how it has changed your life

part3_questions: How has technology changed the way people work?
Do you think older people find it hard to keep up with technology?
Are there any disadvantages of relying too much on technology?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Park or Garden You Like
items.summary: Describe a park or garden that you like to visit.

cue_card.task: Describe a park or garden that you like to visit.
bullets: and explain why you like to visit it

part3_questions: Why are parks important in cities?
Should city land be used for parks or for housing?
How do people's leisure activities in parks differ between generations?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Time You Were Very Busy
items.summary: Describe an occasion when you were very busy.

cue_card.task: Describe an occasion when you were very busy.
bullets: and explain how you felt about being so busy

part3_questions: Do you think people today are busier than in the past?
What are the effects of being too busy?
How can people achieve a better work–life balance?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · Useful Advice You Received
items.summary: Describe a piece of good advice you received.

cue_card.task: Describe a piece of good advice you received.
bullets: and explain why you think it was good advice

part3_questions: Who do young people usually ask for advice?
Is it a good idea to get advice from the internet?
Why do some people find it difficult to accept advice?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Festival or Celebration
items.summary: Describe a festival or celebration that is important in your country.

cue_card.task: Describe a festival or celebration that is important in your country.
bullets: and explain why it is important

part3_questions: Why are traditional festivals important?
Do you think festivals have become too commercial?
How do young people's attitudes to festivals differ from older people's?

items.title: Part 2 & 3 · A Goal for the Future
items.summary: Describe a goal you would like to achieve in the future.

cue_card.task: Describe a goal you would like to achieve in the future.
bullets: what you need to do to achieve it
and explain why this goal is important to you

part3_questions: Is it important for young people to set goals?
What stops people from achieving their goals?
Do you think success is mainly due to hard work or luck?
